subject: surgery
title: Pleomorphic Adenoma, Warthin Tumour, and Salivary Malignancies

steps.tx: Accounting for over seventy percent of all salivary gland neoplasms, **pleomorphic adenoma**, or benign mixed tumor, is the most common tumor of both major and minor salivary glands. It characteristically arises in the superficial lobe of the parotid gland, presenting as a slow-growing, painless, firm, lobulated, mobile swelling at the angle of the jaw. Overlying skin is normal, and facial nerve function remains entirely intact.
steps.say: Pleomorphic adenoma is the most common salivary tumor, presenting as a firm, painless, lobulated mass at the angle of the jaw. Facial nerve function remains completely preserved.

vis.alt: Anatomical schematic and histological diagram of a parotid salivary gland neoplasm.
vis.caption: Parotid gland neoplasm: circumscribed lobulated tumor arising within the superficial parotid lobe. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Histologically, pleomorphic adenoma is a biphasic tumor composed of epithelial and myoepithelial elements embedded within a diverse chondromyxoid or hyaline stroma. The tumor is enveloped by an incomplete pseudocapsule through which microscopic tentacular extensions, known as **capsular pseudopods**, protrude into adjacent normal salivary tissue. Because simple enucleation leaves these microscopic pseudopods behind, leading to high recurrence rates exceeding thirty percent, superficial parotidectomy is the standard operation.
steps.say: Pleomorphic adenoma contains epithelial cells in a chondromyxoid stroma. Microscopic pseudopods penetrate its pseudocapsule, so simple shelling out causes recurrence; superficial parotidectomy is required.

left.title: Simple Enucleation (Unacceptable)
points: Blunt shelling out of tumor along its apparent capsule
Breaches incomplete pseudocapsule during mobilization
Leaves microscopic capsular pseudopods in parotid bed
Prohibitive tumor recurrence rate of twenty to forty percent
Secondary recurrences are characteristically multifocal

right.title: Superficial Parotidectomy (Standard)
points: Formal dissection and visual preservation of facial nerve branches
En bloc excision of entire superficial lobe enclosing tumor intact
Ensures a circumferential margin of normal parotid parenchyma
Long-term tumor recurrence rate drops to under two percent
Prevents catastrophic multifocal surgical bed seeding

steps.tx: Although histologically benign, longstanding or neglected pleomorphic adenomas harbor a defined risk of malignant transformation into **carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma**. Occurring in roughly one to five percent of cases, malignant degeneration increases sharply after ten to fifteen years of tumor presence. Clinical warning signs alerting the surgeon to malignant change include sudden rapid tumor enlargement, onset of deep unremitting pain, skin fixation or ulceration, and the emergence of facial nerve paresis.
steps.say: Neglected pleomorphic adenomas can transform into carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma after years of stability. Sudden rapid growth, unremitting pain, or facial nerve weakness signal malignant change.

rows: Growth Velocity
Indolent, slow expansion over years or decades
Sudden aggressive growth spurt in a preexisting stable lump
Pain and Consistency
Completely painless, rubbery-firm, and mobile
Severe localized pain, rock-hard induration, and tethering
Facial Nerve Status
Always intact (normal symmetrical facial movement)
Ipsilateral lower motor neuron facial weakness or paralysis
Regional Lymph Nodes
Never involved (no regional lymphadenopathy)
Frequent metastatic enlargement of cervical lymph nodes

steps.tx: The second most common benign parotid neoplasm is **Warthin tumour**, historically designated papillary cystadenoma lymphomatosum or adenolymphoma. It occurs almost exclusively within the parotid gland, with over eighty-five percent localized to the lower pole or tail of the superficial lobe. Warthin tumour exhibits a striking demographic predilection for elderly male cigarette smokers and presents with synchronous or metachronous bilateral parotid involvement in ten to fifteen percent of cases.
steps.say: Warthin tumor is a benign parotid lesion arising in the lower tail of the gland, characteristically seen in elderly male smokers. It is bilateral in up to fifteen percent of patients.

left.title: Warthin Tumour (Adenolymphoma)
points: Papillary projections lined by oncocytic double-layered epithelium
Dense lymphoid stroma with active germinal centers
Strong predilection for male cigarette smokers over age fifty
Hot nodule on technetium-99m pertechnetate scan
Essentially zero potential for malignant transformation

right.title: Pleomorphic Adenoma
points: Biphasic epithelial and myoepithelial cells in myxoid stroma
Lacks organized lymphoid tissue or oncocytic papillae
Slight female predominance across broad adult age range
Cold filling defect on technetium-99m scintigraphy
One to five percent risk of transformation into adenocarcinoma

steps.tx: The most common primary malignant salivary neoplasm in both adults and children is **mucoepidermoid carcinoma**, representing over thirty percent of all salivary malignancies. Histologically, it comprises a variable mixture of three distinct cell types: mucin-producing epithelial cells, squamous epidermoid cells, and intermediate progenitor cells. Tumors are categorized as low, intermediate, or high grade based on cellular differentiation, mitotic activity, necrosis, and neural invasion.
steps.say: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is the most common primary salivary malignancy, consisting of mucin-secreting, epidermoid, and intermediate cells. It is graded histologically from low to high grade.

rows: Low-Grade Mucoepidermoid
Predominance of well-differentiated mucin cysts and mature squamoid cells
Behaves indolently, managed with wide excision or superficial parotidectomy alone
Intermediate-Grade
Equal mixture of intermediate cells and mucin-secreting elements
Moderate local recurrence risk, managed with total parotidectomy and neck staging
High-Grade Mucoepidermoid
Predominance of poorly differentiated epidermoid sheets, necrosis, mitoses
Aggressive malignancy mimicking SCC, requires total parotidectomy, neck dissection, and radiation

steps.tx: In minor salivary glands and the submandibular gland, the most prevalent malignancy is **adenoid cystic carcinoma**. On light microscopy, it displays three classical architectural patterns: cribriform, tubular, and solid. The cribriform pattern represents the classic Swiss cheese histology, where malignant epithelial cells encircle round, well-demarcated pseudocystic spaces filled with basophilic basement membrane-like mucinous material. The presence of greater than thirty percent solid architecture portends a dismal prognosis.
steps.say: Adenoid cystic carcinoma exhibits a Swiss-cheese cribriform pattern surrounding mucin-filled spaces. Most common in minor salivary glands, solid variants carry a poor prognosis.

rows: Cribriform Pattern
Classic Swiss-cheese nests surrounding circular mucinous pseudolumina
Intermediate biological aggression with prolonged indolent survival
Tubular Pattern
Well-formed hollow tubules lined by inner ductal and outer myoepithelial cells
Most favorable prognosis among adenoid cystic carcinoma variants
Solid Pattern
Solid sheets of malignant cells lacking lumens or pseudocysts
Highly aggressive with early distant hematogenous metastases and poor survival

steps.tx: The defining hallmark of adenoid cystic carcinoma is its extraordinary affinity for **perineural tracking**, infiltrating miles along nerve sheaths far beyond macroscopic tumor boundaries. It readily tracks retrograde along the facial nerve, lingual nerve, or maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve into the skull base and intracranial cavernous sinus. Because of this relentless neurotropism, patients characteristically complain of deep facial pain or numbness long before a palpable tumor mass is detected.
steps.say: Adenoid cystic carcinoma is notorious for tracking along cranial nerves into the skull base. This pronounced neurotropism causes deep facial pain and numbness early in the disease.

nodes.label: Tracks Centripetally Along CN VII or CN V
Passes Through Stylomastoid or Ovale Foramen

steps.tx: Adenoid cystic carcinoma exhibits a uniquely deceptive biological trajectory characterized by indolent local growth coupled with high rates of **late distant metastasis**. While regional cervical lymph node metastasis occurs in less than ten percent of cases, hematogenous dissemination to the lungs and skeleton develops in over fifty percent of patients, often surfacing ten to twenty years after initial curative surgery. Consequently, patients require extended lifelong pulmonary imaging and clinical surveillance.
steps.say: Adenoid cystic carcinoma rarely metastasizes to neck lymph nodes but spreads through blood vessels to the lungs in over half of cases, often presenting ten to twenty years later.

nodes.label: Indolent Metastatic Progression Allows Extended Survival
